title: Cubical Sheaf Complexes with Constant Expansion with Applications to Asymptotically Good qLTCs
authors: Yeyuan Chen, Miryam Mi-Ying Huang, Yinchen Liu, Er-Cheng Tang
abstract: For every fixed integers $r \ge 4$ and $2 \le k \le r-2$, we construct $r$-dimensional cubical sheaf complexes whose degree-$k$ CSS codes have positive constant rate, linear distance, and constant soundness, with bounded row and column weights. Taking $r=4$ and $k=2$ gives a family of asymptotically good binary qLTCs.   At the core of our construction is a uniform product-expansion theorem for explicit Reed-Solomon codes on norm-one evaluation sets. The key point is that the expansion constant stays bounded away from zero as the local code lengths grow. We place these codes on arithmetic cubical complexes, obtaining constant local expansion for both the resulting sheaf and its dual. Together with the local-to-global framework of Dinur, Lin, and Vidick (FOCS 2024) and sheaf duality, this gives linear distance and constant soundness, while an asymmetric choice of local code dimensions gives positive rate. The resulting codes are explicit and polynomial-time computable.
summary: This paper develops a sophisticated mathematical construction for building quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs) with optimal asymptotic parameters. It achieves this by embedding the coding problem within the framework of cubical sheaf complexes defined over arithmetic quotients of trees. The work is significant for providing explicit, polynomial-time methods to construct highly efficient quantum error correction codes.
main_problem: The primary goal is to construct quantum error correcting codes (qLTCs) that simultaneously achieve constant rate, linear distance, and constant soundness while maintaining bounded local check and qubit degrees.
main_result: The authors present an explicit, polynomial-time computable family of codes derived from $r$-dimensional cubical sheaf complexes, achieving the desired asymptotic bounds for qLTCs.
method: The construction method combines cubical sheaf complexes with a uniform product-expansion theorem applied to Reed-Solomon codes on arithmetic cubical complexes, leveraging the local-to-global framework.
model_or_system: The theoretical model is quantum error correction, specifically focusing on CSS codes derived from the structure of cubical sheaf complexes built upon arithmetic quotients of products of trees.
key_observables: Code parameters such as rate ($K/N$), minimum distance ($D$), and soundness ($ho$), which are shown to be bounded away from zero or linear in $N$.
important_parameters: The construction is parameterized by fixed integers $r \ge 4$ and $2 \le k \le r-2$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the existence of arithmetic quotients of products of trees and the successful establishment of uniform product expansion for the local Reed-Solomon codes and their duals.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the structure of a decorated Cayley cubical complex, detailing how edges and cubes are defined and how opposite edges must agree.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general framework of cubical complexes and sheaf theory, applies this to arithmetic quotients of products of trees, establishes the necessary local coding conditions (product expansion), and culminates in the main theorems proving the existence of the desired quantum codes.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the reliance on complex combinatorial structures (sheaves, complexes) to guarantee robust coding properties is a theoretical advancement that could inspire new ways to analyze error correction in complex quantum systems.
